meta.name: The Farms
meta.blurb: A failing harvest and the roads the warband will come down.

activities.name: Work the failing fields
activities.blurb: The barley came up blighted and thin. Whatever can still be cut is cut, and a hungry town counts every sheaf.

activities.name: Stand at the reeve's ledger
activities.blurb: The manor reeve guards the granary with his great book and a tally of who has eaten and who has not.

activities.name: Watch the outer roads
activities.blurb: Beyond the last field the lanes run empty toward the burning country. Whatever comes for St Sebastian comes by these roads first.

activities.name: Sit with the farmhands
activities.blurb: In the cattle byre the cottars share what little there is and say aloud what the town will not. Hungry men, and angry ones.

events.text: The reeve sets you among the rows with a sickle and a grim instruction: take everything that is not yet rotted, and say nothing the priest might overhear. Half the ears crumble to black dust in your fist before they ever reach the basket.

pass.text: You work the rows till your palms split, sorting the sound grain from the spoiled with a patience the others have lost. By dusk there is a wagon's worth saved where there might have been nothing, and the reeve marks it down without quite bringing himself to thank you.
pass.outcome: salvaged a wagon of sound grain from the blighted fields.

fail.text: The blight has gone deeper than the husk; for every basket you fill, half is fit only for swine, and the reek of it follows you down the rows. You bring in what you can. It is a thin offering, and the reeve's silence says he expected no better, of the harvest or of you.
fail.outcome: brought in a thin, blighted share and little else.

events.text: The reeve runs a cracked nail down his ledger: so many mouths, so many bushels, and the two columns no longer meet however he adds them. He looks up at you, a stranger off the foreign ship, and asks plainly whether you have come to eat his stores or to help fill them.

choices.label: Offer to help bring the granary up

effect.text: You pledge your back to the gleaning and your wits to the count, and something in the old man unclenches. He shows you the empty bins and the full, and where a careful hand might yet make the difference between a fed town and a starved one.
effect.outcome: won the reeve's trust and a hand in the granary.

choices.label: Ask what a stranger gets for the trouble

effect.text: You name your price before you have lifted a finger, and the reeve's face shutters like a barn door against the wind. He gives you a day's bread and not a crumb more, and you feel his eyes follow you out, counting you now among the mouths and not the hands.
effect.outcome: haggled with the reeve and was counted a burden, not a help.

events.text: The reeve hands you the granary keys for one night and a hard task to go with them: every sack of salvaged grain weighed, sorted, and stored against the lean weeks the red-eyed thing in your dreams keeps promising. Get it wrong and the whole town goes short when there is nothing left to spare.

pass.text: You weigh and ledger through the small hours by a guttering lamp, rooting out the spoiled sacks before they can rot the sound, until the bins stand full and squared and counted twice over. When the lean weeks come, St Sebastian will eat a little longer for this one night's work.
pass.outcome: filled and squared the town granary against the hunger to come.

fail.text: The figures swim and the sacks blur, and somewhere in the dark you miscount a bin and leave the rot to spread unseen beneath the good. The reeve finds the spoilage at dawn and takes the keys back without a word, and a portion of the town's bread is lost before the hunger has even begun.
fail.outcome: fumbled the granary count and let good grain spoil.

events.text: You walk the outer lanes where the carriers' carts used to rattle by daily. The road is silent now, the verges grown wild, and on the far hills a single thread of smoke stands where a village ought to be. The country is emptying, and it is emptying toward you.

pass.text: You read the road the way a tracker reads a wood: ruts gone cold, milestones unswept, a child's shoe left in the ditch with no child anywhere near it. Whatever drove these people off is coming this way, and you mark the pace of it days before the town will let itself believe you — and days of warning are days to make the walls ready.
pass.outcome: read the empty roads and guessed the ruin coming toward St Sebastian.

fail.text: You walk a long way and learn little that a frightened farmer could not have told you: the roads are empty, the smoke is real. You turn back at dusk no wiser than you set out, the dread sitting heavy in you with no shape you can give it and no name.
fail.outcome: walked the empty roads and came back with only dread.

events.text: A lone rider keeps to the treeline at the field's edge, counting the town's walls and gates with a soldier's eye, then wheeling his horse to ride back the way he came. A scout, plainly, for something far larger behind him. He has not yet seen you crouched low in the stubble.

pass.text: You take him out of the saddle in the high barley before he can cry out, a knee on his chest and his own knife at his throat. He is half-starved under his mail, and terrified, and you have him bound and dragged to the byre before the light fails. The warband has lost its eyes on the town. He will talk.
pass.outcome: ran down the warband's scout and took him alive.

fail.text: Your boot finds a dry furrow and the crack of it turns his head; he is spurring away before you have cleared the rows, low over the horse's neck and gone into the dusk. He carries the count of the walls and gates back to his masters, and worse, you know for certain the town is being watched.
fail.outcome: lost the scout and let the count of the walls ride back to the warband.

events.text: The bound scout sweats in the byre's lamplight, the fever already bright behind his eyes. The farmhands want him hanged from the rafter where he sits; you want what he carries in his skull. He licks his cracked lips and offers to trade the truth for water and a clean death.

choices.label: Give him water and hear him out

effect.text: He drinks, and then he talks: a warband of the dying, hundreds strong, sick men with nothing left to lose and nothing left to fear, marching on St Sebastian for its walls and its stores. He gives you their numbers, their road, their days of march. It is the warning the town has refused to hear, and now you carry it whole.
effect.outcome: drew the truth from the scout and laid the warband bare.

choices.label: Let the farmhands have their hanging

effect.text: You step back and the cottars do the rest, and the scout dies cursing in a tongue not one of you knows. The byre is grimly satisfied, and you have made yourself their man, but whatever he knew of the host at his back swings now from the rafter, gone past all asking.
effect.outcome: let the farmhands hang the scout and lost what he knew.

events.text: The farmhands pass a single loaf six ways and talk low about the castle hoarding grain behind its walls while the fields fail. They eye you sidelong, the foreigner who came in on the cursed ship, and an old ploughman asks whether you have come to lord it over them like the rest, or to stand at their shoulder.

pass.text: You take the smallest share of the loaf and lay out your own grievance plain, and by the second round of thin ale they have decided you are one of their own. These are hard hands and harder backs, and if it ever comes to defending the fields, they will look to you to lead them.
pass.outcome: won the farmhands' trust over a shared loaf.

fail.text: You misjudge the room and put one word too soft on the lord, and the byre goes cold around you in an instant. The loaf passes from hand to hand without ever reaching yours, and the old ploughman turns his shoulder, and his talk, away from the stranger in their midst.
fail.outcome: lost the byre's room with one wrong word.

events.text: With the warband's smoke now plain on the hills, you put it to the farmhands straight: scythes can be set straight on poles, billhooks ground sharp, hayforks turned to spears. They are not soldiers, and never will be, but they are many, and they are angry, and they have nowhere left in the world to run.

pass.text: You spend two days between the smithy and the byre, lashing blades to shafts and drilling frightened men into something that holds a line. By the end they stand in rough ranks with edged tools and grim faces, a militia of farmhands ready to hold the fields. It is not much. It may be enough.
pass.outcome: forged the farmhands into an armed militia for the walls.

fail.text: The hafts split, the lashings slip, and the men handle the makeshift spears like the farm tools they have always been. You arm them after a fashion, but a fashion is all it is, and you both know that the first true charge will scatter them across the stubble like chaff.
fail.outcome: armed the farmhands poorly and prayed it would not be tested.

events.text: They come up the lanes you once walked empty: a column of refugees, gaunt and grey, with children who do not cry because they have not the strength left to cry. They can smell the granary on the wind. The reeve looks to you, the keys cold in his hand, and the whole hungry winter hangs on what you say next.

choices.label: Bar the granary and turn them away

effect.text: You take the keys and turn the lock, and tell the column there is nothing here for them. There is, of course; it is behind the very door you have just barred against them. The grain will see St Sebastian through, and the strangers on the road are not St Sebastian's, you tell yourself, over and over, until you very nearly believe it.
effect.outcome: barred the granary and turned the starving refugees away.

choices.label: Open the stores and feed them

effect.text: You break out the bread you laboured to store and the column falls upon it weeping into the dirt. The reeve does not stop you; perhaps he no longer can. You have spent the town's hard margin in one afternoon of mercy, but the hunger camped on St Sebastian's roads breaks like a fever, and no child died at your locked door today.
effect.outcome: opened the stores and fed the starving at the town's own cost.

events.text: The warband's outriders no longer trouble to hide. They sit their horses openly on the rise above the fields at dawn, counting heads and weighing the walls, close enough now that you can see the plague rotting them in the saddle. Behind them the smoke is no longer a distant thread. The reckoning the red eyes foretold is days away, perhaps only hours.

effect.text: You stand in the cold stubble and watch them watch the town, and feel the dream-vision settle at last over the waking world: the city will fall, as all cities have fallen. You carry the count of them back through the gates while the light still holds, and whatever St Sebastian does now, it does with its eyes open.
effect.outcome: watched the warband's outriders gather and carried the warning in.
